A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ICP research despite the revised title. Their text, equations, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including Appendices A–B in v1 and A–C in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on Guessing Number, Revealing Goals, and Hanabi, plus a Hanabi embedding-shuffling analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds comparative results for two DIAL variants and an ICP Hanabi win-rate result.

M1.justification: The ICP architecture, action/message policies, random and delayed mapping approaches, Gumbel-Softmax training, and hat mapping are retained. The newly evaluated ICN-DIAL-DM instantiates the already described delayed-map approach; it does not introduce a new ICP component.

E1.justification: The same three base tasks remain, with Guessing Number renamed Guessing Numbers. However, v2 adds a direct-channel condition for the two synthetic tasks: DIAL-Cheat can broadcast messages while taking environment actions, changing communication availability within those existing games (Appendix A.3).

E2.justification: The Guessing Numbers and Revealing Goals comparisons expand from ICN and two VDN baselines to five approaches, adding DIAL-Cheat and ICN-DIAL-DM. Existing ICN is renamed ICN-DIAL-RM. The Hanabi comparator set is retained after matching the RM/DM naming changes.

E3.justification: Appendix A.3 specifies protocols for the added comparisons: a discrete channel sized to the scouting-action space, and ICN-DIAL-DM pretraining with scouting actions removed before transfer and fine-tuning. Appendix C adds Hanabi win rate as an outcome metric. Existing task sizes, training-step settings, and principal hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figures 2–3 newly compare random-map and delayed-map training using DIAL on both synthetic tasks, alongside a direct-channel reference, providing additional evidence about communication and training choices. The six-embedding Hanabi sensitivity analysis is retained; moving Figure 4 to the appendix does not constitute a new analysis.

E5.justification: Figure 2(b) adds error bars to episode-length results, including the retained methods whose bars previously displayed only means. The error-bar statistic is not defined. Six-seed reporting for the synthetic experiments and selection of the best Hanabi runs from more than three seeds remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Figures 2–3 add DIAL-Cheat and ICN-DIAL-DM results; Figure 2(b) reports episode lengths of 6.65 and 9.35, respectively, while ICN-DIAL-RM retains 8.63. Figures 2(a) and 3(a) also exchange the VDN on/off-policy curve labels. Appendix C newly reports 91% ICP wins and cites 41.45% for SAD; the reported Hanabi mean scores remain 24.91 and 23.81.

T1.justification: The Dec-POMDP formulation, scouting-action definitions, Equation (1), value decomposition, and Gumbel-Softmax expressions are substantively unchanged. Appendix C's near-maximum-performance interpretation supplies no new mathematical bound or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: communication through scouting-action mappings, two training approaches, and improved coordination on the three tasks. The headline Hanabi performance claim is unchanged; the revised title does not establish a different scientific contribution.

C2.justification: New Appendix C explains that Hanabi's score ceiling can conceal a large win-rate difference, discusses near-24 scores in unsuccessful games, and elaborates the near-maximum-performance interpretation using starting-hand constraints. The existing limitation concerning environments without scouting actions remains.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds implementation information for DIAL-Cheat and ICN-DIAL-DM, including message cardinality, simultaneous messaging and acting, removal of scouting actions during pretraining, and subsequent fine-tuning. Existing network descriptions, Algorithm 1, hardware information, hyperparameters, and the supplementary-code availability statement are retained.

R1.justification: Section 5.2 adds six references on hat games, including Brown and Tanton and Butler et al., attributing the existing hat-mapping mechanism more explicitly. The broader positioning relative to MARL communication and theory-of-mind methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 revises the title, standardizes RM/DM variant names and Guessing Numbers terminology, and makes grammatical edits throughout. It adds Appendices A.3 and C and acknowledgements, while retaining the main section sequence and most existing exposition.

P2.justification: v2 reformats the document throughout in ICLR style, changing the title/author arrangement, running headers, text width, typography, and figure sizing. Figures 2–3 gain series and revised legends/axes, Figure 2(b) expands to five bars with error bars, and Figure 4 moves from the main text to the appendix.

improvement.justification: The added comparisons in Figures 2–3 and implementation instructions in Appendix A.3 provide useful evidence about training choices and improve reproducibility. Appendix C adds win-rate context to the retained Hanabi scores. These gains are limited by undefined error bars, unexplained VDN curve relabeling, and continued best-run selection for Hanabi; the core method and headline results remain unchanged.
